statement: Assemble a virtual cell from a preset robot, tools, references, parts, signals and a controller, with aliases matching the real machine.

source.ref: Cell panel (Robot, Create Reference, Create Part, Create Tool, Controller, Create Signal)

superiority: Cell as a single reusable object with named, diffable configuration instead of loose components.

acceptance.corpus: Cell with robot, tool, 2 references and 3 parts saved and reloaded
acceptance.tolerance: All entities round-trip with identical poses (<= 1e-6 mm)

statement: Create a tool from a body mesh, mounting frame and TCP frame and attach it to the robot, with part mass included in the tool total.
superiority: Compute mass and centre of gravity from the solid directly and warn on payload overruns.

acceptance.corpus: Tool solid with known volume and density
acceptance.tolerance: Computed mass within 0.1% of analytic; payload warning raised above limit

statement: Create references with optional parents and an in-world switch so targets move with, or stay fixed against, a work frame.
superiority: Re-anchor all targets when a reference is touched up, with a visible delta report.

acceptance.corpus: Reference shifted by 12 mm and rotated 3 deg
acceptance.tolerance: All dependent targets update to <= 0.01 mm of rigid transform

statement: Model a positioner from parts, fixed connections and revolute joints with limits, flange endpoint and assemble it into a mechanism that the solver drives together with the robot.
superiority: Joint optimisation of robot plus mechanism axes to avoid singularities and limits.

acceptance.corpus: Robot on linear track following a 6 m line
acceptance.tolerance: TCP error <= 0.05 mm; track position monotonic and within limits

statement: Create Cartesian targets from frames, joint-space targets from joint values and targets from curves.
superiority: Tag-based labels that follow geometry and survive model edits.

acceptance.corpus: 100 targets from curve frames with names
acceptance.tolerance: Names preserved and pose error <= 0.001 mm

statement: Set motion space (Cartesian line or arc versus joint), speed and acceleration limits and blend radius for moves.
superiority: Visualize resulting velocity and blend per segment on the path.

acceptance.corpus: Toolpath with 3 setting groups
acceptance.tolerance: Per-segment settings reproduced in output; durations within 1% of analytic

statement: Chain actions such as moves, waits and signal changes into procedures and inspect the resulting sequence in a procedure browser.
superiority: Toolpath history with undo and non-destructive edits.

acceptance.corpus: Concatenate 5 procedures and reverse one
acceptance.tolerance: Action order and attributes match the expected sequence

statement: Declare digital or analogue input and output signals with alias and voltage states, bind them to the controller and change their state from procedure steps.
superiority: Keep indices consistent across cells via named signals and check mapping at export time.

acceptance.corpus: Program using 8 digital outputs mapped 0- to 1-based
acceptance.tolerance: All indices correct on export for ABB and UR

statement: Insert verbatim controller code lines and timed or synchronisation waits into procedures, with an optional separate behaviour for simulation.
superiority: Typed, debuggable procedure graph with step-through in simulation.

acceptance.corpus: Procedure with 5 custom code actions and a 2 s wait
acceptance.tolerance: Exported code contains the 5 lines verbatim in order; simulation shows the wait only

notes: Loops and conditions are marked Coming Soon in the official tutorial; they are not claimed here.

statement: Solve a procedure on the virtual cell, replay it, and report notifications for unreachable or problematic positions before export.
superiority: Highlight the exact segment and cause, and propose joint-limit-safe alternatives.

acceptance.corpus: Path with 10 seeded singularities and 8 unreachable targets
acceptance.tolerance: All 18 found; no false positives on clean targets

notes: Docs state the solver reports issues as notifications; singularity-specific detection is not described and is not confirmed against official docs.

statement: Export a procedure as controller-native code (RAPID, KRL, VAL) in inline or predeclaration style, with per-path settings for multi-robot and external axes.
superiority: Parse-verify exported files with a per-brand checker.

acceptance.corpus: Same procedure exported for ABB, KUKA, UR and Staubli
acceptance.tolerance: Zero parse errors; poses within 0.001 mm

statement: Generate the program in the target controller language by configuring the virtual controller version and subsystems for ABB RAPID, KUKA KRL or Universal Robots URScript.

source.ref: Configure a Virtual Controller / language subsystems

superiority: Report per-language capability differences before switching.

acceptance.corpus: 50-target program converted across three languages
acceptance.tolerance: Equal TCP poses in all outputs within 0.01 mm

statement: Upload a generated program to an ABB controller in automatic mode through RobotWare Web Services or PCSDK, with an optional auto-run.
superiority: Show upload preflight (mode, task, diff) and rollback.

acceptance.corpus: Mock ABB service receiving a 500-line module
acceptance.tolerance: Uploaded bytes hash-equal; mode violations refused

statement: Upload and execute a URScript program on a Universal Robots controller through its dashboard server with remote control enabled, plus manual file load as an alternative.
superiority: Verify controller state and safety mode before upload.

acceptance.corpus: Mock UR dashboard accepting load/play commands
acceptance.tolerance: Commands acknowledged in order; refuse when remote control off

statement: Stream state to and from an ABB controller through its EGM subsystem and monitor Universal Robots controllers and their signals through RTDE.
superiority: Deterministic latency budget with timestamped logs and replay.

acceptance.corpus: Mock controller stream at 100 Hz for 60 s
acceptance.tolerance: Median latency <= 30 ms; no dropped frames in replay

notes: Latency targets come from the acceptance test, not the docs; the ABB page lists EGM capabilities Monitor, Stream and Receive State, and the UR page lists RTDE monitoring and signal read/write.

statement: Represent each controller as a version plus toggleable capabilities (upload, execution, signal read) implemented by selectable subsystems.
superiority: Report which capabilities a target controller lacks at authoring time.

acceptance.corpus: Capability matrix for 4 controllers
acceptance.tolerance: Missing capabilities flagged before export; none missed

statement: Search and browse component documentation by keyword from a canvas component, preview overloads and add components to the document.
superiority: Offline, fuzzy-searchable component help with runnable examples.

acceptance.corpus: 50 keyword queries for known components
acceptance.tolerance: Correct component in top 3 for >= 95% of queries

statement: Reuse or rename existing controller variables for tools, references and signals during export using alias suffix syntax to force, skip or rename declarations.
superiority: Dino 8 maps existing controller variables through a visible table instead of alias syntax.

acceptance.corpus: Alias set to force, skip and rename on 3 tools
acceptance.tolerance: Exported code declares or omits each variable as specified in 100% of cases

statement: Synchronise motion of several mechanisms with shared sync settings so their moves start together and share a duration.
superiority: Dino 8 validates sync groups before solving and shows the shared timeline.

acceptance.corpus: Two robots with 5 synchronised moves each
acceptance.tolerance: Durations equal within 1 ms; unequal action counts rejected with message

statement: Couple one mechanism to another with primary and secondary roles and target resolvers such as vector-aligned axes so a positioner or track follows the robot targets.
superiority: Dino 8 solves coupled kinematics with joint-limit awareness shown live.

acceptance.corpus: Track and robot following a 6 m line
acceptance.tolerance: TCP error under 0.05 mm; track position within limits

statement: Attach, detach and switch the active endpoint of tools at runtime within a procedure.
superiority: Dino 8 shows mass and TCP changes in the timeline.

acceptance.corpus: Procedure with 3 tool changes and a two-endpoint tool
acceptance.tolerance: Active TCP after each change equals expected frame within 1e-6 mm

statement: Mount a robot on a linear track and program track and robot together, with export mapping of the extra axis after the robot axes.
superiority: Dino 8 exports external axes from the same document without separate extension plug-ins.

acceptance.corpus: Robot on a 6 m track
acceptance.tolerance: Joint mapping index equals robot axis count; export parses without error

statement: Realign targets with transform modifiers (parallel to a vector, free transform) and drop redundant targets by position and orientation tolerance.
superiority: Dino 8 previews target edits in the viewport with undo.

acceptance.corpus: Curve-derived 500 targets with 10 percent near-duplicates
acceptance.tolerance: Remaining and discarded sets partition input exactly; discarded within tolerance of neighbours

statement: Replace theoretical tool or reference frames with calibrated controller values entered as position and quaternion in the controller unit.
superiority: Dino 8 imports calibration data from controller files.

acceptance.corpus: Calibrated TCP with quaternion given in mm
acceptance.tolerance: Frame equals source values within 1e-6; targets re-solved at the calibrated TCP

statement: Assemble tools from several parts and named connections with multiple endpoints such as camera and gripper centre points.
superiority: Dino 8 checks endpoint frames for orientation consistency.

acceptance.corpus: Tool with three parts and two endpoints
acceptance.tolerance: Endpoint frames match the model within 1e-6 mm

statement: Coordinate several robots without synchronising their motion by waiting on shared sync settings.
superiority: Dino 8 detects deadlocks between waits before export.

acceptance.corpus: Two robots with matched wait-sync actions
acceptance.tolerance: Second robot waits until the first reaches the sync point; unmatched wait reported

statement: Test generated programs against simulated controllers such as RobotStudio loopback and URSim before using real hardware.

source.ref: Simulation setups for ABB and UR

superiority: Dino 8 bundles its own controller emulator needing no vendor install.

acceptance.corpus: Upload of 500-line program to simulator
acceptance.tolerance: Program received and run to completion; failures logged with reason
